recipes.name: Spinach and Mushroom Quiche with Shiitake Mushrooms
ingredients_raw: 1 slice turkey bacon, cut into 1/2-inch pieces

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Fit pie crust into a 9-inch pie dish.

Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat; cook and stir green onions and garlic until green onions are softened, about 5 minutes. Cook and stir turkey bacon in green onion mixture until fragrant.
Stir spinach, shiitake mushrooms, and broccoli into green onion mixture; cook and stir vegetables until softened, 5 to 7 minutes. Mix in 1/4 cup Cheddar cheese.
Spoon vegetable mixture into pie crust.
Beat eggs, milk, sea salt, and black pepper together in a bowl; pour egg mixture gently over vegetable filling, slightly stirring eggs into filling to combine.

Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes; sprinkle 1/2 cup Cheddar cheese over the top of quiche and bake 10 additional minutes. Cover quiche with aluminum foil and bake until quiche has set and a toothpick inserted into it comes out clean, about 10 more minutes.
Allow quiche to cool for 5 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Spinach and Mushroom Quiche with Shiitake Mushrooms
raw_recipe.description: This savory egg quiche is a mouthwatering combination of fresh spinach, shiitake mushrooms, broccoli, turkey bacon, and sharp Cheddar cheese.

review.reviewBody: Great recipe! The shiitake mushrooms were fantastic. I also added a bit of goat cheese that I had lying around and needed to use up. It was a good idea!

Great recipe that leaves room for substitutions. I think the secret to the success of this quiche is the fact that you cook the spinach and mushrooms before putting them into the crust. I recommend using a slotted spoon to do so, in order to avoid putting the water that cooks out of the vegetable mixture into the crust—that will ensure the crust doesn’t get soggy while cooking. I also put the first 1/4 cup of cheddar onto the vegetables after putting them into the crust (not before) so that it didn’t get mixed into the water. Crimini (baby portobello) mushrooms work well in this if you don’t have shiitake.

This was a great recipe. I made several changes based on ingredients I had on hand and to make it more savory. I used coarsely chopped kale and onion instead of spinach and broccoli. I sauted the veggies with basil butter, savory, and thyme. I did not mix the cheese with the vegetables. Instead I sprinkled feta and cheddar on top of the vegetables. The feta made the flavor more complex and intense. I mixed chives with the egg/milk and used half the salt and a little less milk. I didn't cover the quiche for the last 10 min to allow the crust and cheese to brown and crisp. This was the best quiche I've ever made and I'll definitely use shiitakes again.

Have made it several times, do change up the veggies to what I have on hand. Yes do need to use a deep dish pie plate. I pre cook all and then mix it up in pan and then put in pie plate. So I love this quiche!!

This was an easy recipe and I added/changed ingredients. I used baby bella mushrooms, some pork breakfast sausage sliced in small rounds, and a dash of cayenne for spice. Baking at a mile high, once the dish was covered with aluminum foil, I ended up extending the cooking time about 15 minutes to get a toothpick to come out clean. My wife loved it!

I didn't have all the ingredients, but the volume of ingredients was nearly the same. I used 5oz mushrooms, 1/2 onion, 1/2 cup broccoli, no green onion or bacon. I used 1/2c cheese with the veggies instead of 1/4c, and put a heaping 1/2c more when called for during the last 10 minutes. I also substituted half and half for the milk. This fit perfectly in a 9" deep dish frozen pie crust. I did do as another poster said and removed the foil after the 10 minutes and put it back in for another 5 minutes since it wasn't quite done. I also wanted it hotter so I left it in 3 minutes more so an extra 8 minutes total. My husband raved about it. Oh...and I used a mixture of cheddar and gouda. Just devine. I didn't get a photo before cutting. Oops

The first time I made this, I unintentionally altered the recipe. Not owning a pie plate at the time, I bought a pre-made pie crust that came in a shallow pie plate. As such there wasn't enough room for all the spinach the recipe called for. I made it and it was awesome. 5 stars!

After making this for a while, I decided to get a real pie plate and make it again. The result... 4 stars. The spinach was a bit overpowering compared to the taste that I was now used to. The way I make it now is that I double the onions, bacon, mushroom, broccoli, and mixed in cheese. The result... 5 stars again. :)

I also tried using non-baby spinach once and that was a mistake. Baby spinach is the way to go every time. Bon appetit!

Terrific!! Didn’t want to buy a package of turkey bacon to use 1 slice called for in this recipe. Instead, added a heaping teaspoon of bacon grease to give this some ‘bacon’ flavor, and eliminated the 1/4 cup butter. Stirring the egg mixture into the vegetable mixture after it was placed into the pie shell seemed like an opportunity to damage the crust. Poured about 1/3 of the egg mixture into the vegetables, and then spooned the combined mixture into the pie shell with the remaining egg mixture poured into the shell. The last ten minute baking time increment, with the quiche foiled, had to be extended an extra 6 minutes to get a clean toothpick. Will make this again soon as the hungry clan devoured this quiche in a flash.

Great recipe. I was able to fill two deep dish pie crust with the veggies and made an extra batch of the egg mixture to have two beautiful, colorful quiches. I didn't add the bacon, instead used extra mushrooms. Will definitely make again.
I didn't have turkey bacon and substitute hickory bacon which should have been cooked first before the green onions; if using regular bacon needs to be crispy!! But not sure I will try again!
This was an easy recipe and the kids loved it. I substituted a mixture of gouda and swiss instead of the cheddar and used Morningstar bacon to make it vegetarian, it turned out great!

I have made this recipe, sometimes with variations, for the last 5 years approximately 50 times. It is a great lunch for Sundays. I usually use bella mushrooms and 1/2 and 1/2 light cream in the place of milk.
V enjoyable! Made with cauliflower instead of broccoli, proportions seemed good for everything considering a quiche. It helped to cut vegetables before cooking for timing.
I only used spinach and mushroom with bacon bites. It is delicious.
I love this recipe I come back to it time and again. I use Italian blend cheeses instead of cheddar though.
Loved it! Cooked it in my Nuwave oven
Fantastic quiche. I make four quiches at a time. I use less cheese, to be slightly more heart healthy, and it turns out just as good.

I love this recipe and use it all the time. I rarely follow the recipe exactly... switching out veggies or using mandolin sliced potatoes par-baked in the pie dish instead of a crust... but I never make a quiche without pulling this recipe up for the ratios and spot-on cooking directions/ technique. It’s delicious made as-is, but a great recipe to get creative with too. Thank you!

Loved this recipe! I made it as directed, but used regular bacon and instead of broccoli I used frozen peas (personal taste). Also I used a combination of cheddar cheese and shredded Parmesan because it was what I had on hand. Will definitely make this again.
Awesome paired with a salad!
